anchor.statement: Proposition 6.6. Each class in Section 6.4 is closed under finite sums at a fixed exponent. For α , β ∈ R , products satisfy M α M β ⊂ M α + β , M α W β ⊂ W α + β . (6.30) For a γ ,m ∈ W α and b γ ,m′ ∈ W β with the same label, a γ ,m b γ ,m ′ ∈ {︄ W α + β , m + m ′ ̸= 0, with harmonic m + m ′ , M α + β , m + m ′ = 0, after temporal cutoff. (6.31) Before cutoff, a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle. Actual waves with distinct labels satisfy, for every pair of derivative multi-indices I, J, ( ∂ I w γ )( ∂ J w γ ′ ) = 0 ( γ ̸= γ ′ ). For C ∈ {M, W}, every coefficient derivative in a fixed common-torus representative preserves the ε exponent in its defining bounds. The operators below also preserve (6.20) and therefore act on the classes by operator mapping ∂ R,Z,T C α −→ C α D r C α −→ C α − κs D z = ε∂ Z C α −→ C α +1 Q 1+h N abs = c i 0 N i 0 C α −→ C α − ε∂ T C α −→ C α +1 . (6.32) These mappings concern amplitudes with the phase factored out. The local coordinate derivative bounds, including those for ∂ H , retain the prescribed supports. The wave rules are local to the labelled rectangles before cutoff, and hold for smoothly extended fields on the common torus after cutoff. Products, differentiation, and angular averaging preserve finite band-independent harmonic sets at every fixed stage.

correspondence.note: The Lean classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) record only the weighted derivative bounds; descent to the common torus, (6.20), supports and smooth zero extension are carried by separate lemmas. Stated directly: sums, M_α M_β ⊂ M_(α+β), M_α W_β ⊂ W_(α+β), products of two waves in M_(α+β), the D_r, D_z, −ε∂_T and fast-time rows for mean coefficients, harmonic addition, the zero-harmonic average and finite harmonic sets. The reviewer combines these: the m + m′ ≠ 0 wave case needs bilinear plus the weight comparison ζP² ≤ √ζP; the wave rows of (6.32) instantiate the generic MemClass rules; vanishing of (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ′) combines the value-level supported_cross_product_zero with jet_zero_off_tsupport; and compatibility comes from the pull-back commutation identities.
